title: Corporate Event Planning Kit
subtitle: For HR, marketing, and operations teams running conferences, galas, client dinners, and team events.
intro: Corporate events succeed when the goals are clear, the logistics are tight, and the guest experience feels effortless. This kit walks you from the first brief to post-event ROI, with checklists for venues, AV, registration, accessibility, and dietary needs. Use it to keep stakeholders aligned and vendors accountable.

sections.heading: Event Brief and Goals Worksheet
sections.note: Complete this first and get sign-off from your stakeholders before you book anything.
fields: Event name and format (conference, dinner, retreat, launch)
Target audience and invitee list size
Required speakers or guests of honor

sections.heading: Corporate Event Timeline
sections.note: Adjust for event size. Conferences with 300 or more guests often need 6 to 9 months of lead time.

Pick two or three possible dates, avoiding major Chicago conventions, holidays, and school breaks.

Book keynote speakers, hosts, and talent.
Launch the registration page and open the invitation.
Book catering and confirm menu direction.
Reserve AV, staging, and lighting vendors.
Reserve rentals: tables, chairs, linens, tent, lounge furniture, and signage.
Plan transportation and parking for attendees.
Negotiate a hotel room block if guests travel.
Confirm the agenda, session titles, and speaker bios.
Collect speaker slides and AV requirements.
Send reminders and track registration numbers weekly.
Order printed materials, badges, and swag.
Plan the accessibility and dietary processes.
Secure photography, video, and social media coverage.
Finalize the floor plan, room layouts, and seating.
Send attendee logistics emails with parking, dress code, and agenda.
Confirm headcount estimates with the caterer.
Hold a vendor coordination call to align on load-in and rehearsal.
Print signage, name badges, and seating charts.
Test the registration and check-in system.
Send the final headcount to catering, venue, and rental partners.
Distribute the run of show to staff, vendors, and speakers.
Confirm emergency contacts and a safety plan.
Assign staff roles and shifts.
Prepare onsite kits and registration materials.
Check the weather and arrange a rain plan for any outdoor component.
Confirm every vendor arrival time.
Walk the venue and test all AV equipment.
Brief the staff and volunteers.
Rehearse key sessions and speeches.
Prepare the final attendee list at registration.
Pack the emergency kit.
Arrive early for load-in and setup.
Inspect the rental delivery and count items.
Run a final tech check.
Open registration before the first attendee arrives.

sections.heading: Venue Questions
items: What is the maximum capacity for each room in theater, banquet, and reception styles?
What is included in the rental fee, and what is extra?
Is there a food and beverage minimum, and can we bring in outside catering?
What AV equipment is included, and can we bring our own vendor?
What are the load-in and load-out times, and is there a freight elevator?
Is there reliable Wi-Fi for the expected number of devices, and what is the bandwidth?
Are there power drops and enough outlets in each room?
What are the accessibility features: ramps, elevators, restrooms, and parking?
What is the policy on signage, banners, and branded displays?
Is there on-site parking, valet, or nearby garage pricing?
What is the cancellation and rescheduling policy?
Do you require certificates of insurance from vendors?

sections.heading: AV and Room Setup Styles
sections.note: Space per person is approximate. Always confirm with your venue and rental company.
rows: Chairs only. Add a stage and podium.
6 ft tables and chairs facing front.
60 in or 66 in rounds with linens.
Tables in a U with chairs on the outside.
Tables in a square, chairs around the outside.
Rounds with chairs on one side only.

groups.title: Registration setup
items: Choose a registration platform that handles tickets, payments, and attendee data.
Create a clear registration form that captures name, company, dietary needs, and accessibility needs.
Set up confirmation emails with a calendar invite and event details.
Include a code of conduct and photography policy.
Set a registration cutoff date.
Create a waitlist process if you reach capacity.

groups.title: Check-in prep
items: Print badges alphabetically or by company.
Prepare a list of VIPs, speakers, and sponsors who need special handling.
Set up check-in tables with signs and a clear queue.
Provide a separate line for on-site registration.
Test the scanners, tablets, and Wi-Fi at the check-in area.
Create a backup paper list in case technology fails.

groups.title: On the day
items: Open registration at least 30 minutes before the start.
Greet each attendee and hand out the badge, agenda, and any swag.
Direct attendees to coat check, restrooms, and the first session.
Track no-shows and walk-ins in real time.
Assign a floater to solve any problems quickly.
Close registration after the first session begins and reconcile the list.

sections.heading: Budget per Person
sections.note: Typical split for a seated evening event. Rough Chicago-area guidance only. Costs vary by venue, season, and format.

lines.tip: Include tables, chairs, linens, tent, staging, and lighting. Get an all-in quote.
Confirm service charge, gratuity, and tax in the per-person price.
Include microphones, projection, lighting, and a technician on site.
Negotiate travel costs and overtime in the contract.
Prioritize clear directional signage and branded badges.
Platform fees often scale by ticket.
Hold this until the event is over.

groups.title: Accessibility
items: Ask about accessibility needs on the registration form.
Choose a venue with step-free entry, accessible restrooms, and elevators.
Leave 36 in minimum clear paths between tables and chairs.
Reserve accessible seating near the front and aisle seats for those who need them.
Provide large-print agendas and captioning or sign language interpreters when requested.
Offer a quiet room for guests who need a break.
Reserve accessible parking spaces close to the entrance.
Train staff on how to assist guests respectfully.

groups.title: Dietary needs
items: Collect dietary requirements and allergies in advance.
Offer vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, and nut-free options.
Label every dish clearly with ingredients and major allergens.
Separate prep and serving utensils for allergen-free dishes.
Provide kosher, halal, or other specialized meals if requested.
Brief the catering team on severe allergies.
Mark special meals on the seating chart and badges.
Offer water, non-alcoholic drinks, and coffee at all times.

groups.title: Collect data
items: Send a short survey within 48 hours with 5 to 8 questions.
Record final attendance against registrations and no-show rate.
Track leads generated, meetings booked, or deals influenced.
Collect social media mentions and photos.
Gather vendor and staff feedback.

groups.title: Measure results
items: Compare actual spend with the budget and note variances.
Calculate cost per attendee and cost per qualified lead.
Compare outcomes with the goals set in the brief.
Identify the top three sessions or moments from feedback.
Identify the top three problems and root causes.

groups.title: Report and follow up
items: Send thank-you emails to attendees, speakers, and sponsors.
Share a summary report with key stakeholders within two weeks.
Add notes to the contact database and assign follow-up tasks.
Update the event playbook with lessons learned.
Archive contracts, invoices, and photos for future events.
